newsitem.title: USA: Personal bankruptcies surge in California - report.
newsitem.headline: Personal bankruptcies surge in California - report.

text.p: The number of personal bankruptcy filings rose nearly 35 percent in California last year, with Los Angeles County showing the sharpest year-over-year increase, a report said Tuesday.

Chapter 7 and Chapter 13 filings, the vast majority of which are personal bankruptcies, totaled 177,034 last year, up 34.9 percent from 131,198 for the year before, Santa Ana-based CDB Infotek said in its report.
Chapter 11 filings, typically used by businesses, totaled 1,634 last year, down 19.9 percent from 2,041 for the year before, CDB Infotek said.

"While part of the increase in personal bankruptcies can be attributed to an increased acceptance of bankruptcy as a financial tool, it's clear that a lot of California households haven't shared in the state's economic recovery," said Rick Rozar, CDB Infotek's president and chief executive officer. "There's still a lot of financial hardship out there."

Of the state's major counties, Los Angeles saw the strongest year-over-year increase in personal bankruptcies. Last year there were 53,865 Chapters 7 and 13 filings in Los Angeles County, up 64.2 percent from 32,804 for 1995.
At the other end of the scale, Santa Barbara and El Dorado counties both experienced declines in personal bankruptcies.
CDB Infotek provides on-line access to public records nationwide.
